title: Getting around
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: ʿafwan + , + kayfa adhhab ilā + al- + N?

rules.text: kayfa adhhab ilā…? asks the way without conjugating anything new: kayfa is M2's, adhhab is M4's and ilā is M4's, all from the level below. Only the destination changes.
Direction phrases hang off ʿalā: ʿalā al-yamīn, ʿalā al-yasār. The bare yamīn and yasār are the sides themselves, and the phrase is what points at them.
bi- means "by" as well as "with" and "for": bi-al-ḥāfila is by bus. It is the same bi- that has been sitting inside bi-khayr since M2 and bi-kam since M8, and this is where it is finally explained.
Elision is never written. bi-al-ḥāfila is said bil-ḥāfila and written in full, because a course that wrote both would have two words for one.

The MSA word for a bus is al-ḥāfila, and every passenger in every Arab city says al-bāṣ. This course writes the MSA one everywhere the index can see, and names the other in words here — the only place in the module it appears.

sentences.cue: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?

words.note: Feminine: al-maḥaṭṭa. The ṭ is emphatic and doubled, which is why the word sits low and long in the mouth.

sentences.trap: The whole question is built from words the course already has. Nothing here is new except the place, which is what makes it worth memorising as a frame.
sentences.sound: al-ma-ḤAṬ-ṭa, with the ṭ held twice as long as a single one.

variations.cue: Excuse me, how do I get to the market?
variations.changed: another destination

variations.display: law samaḥta, kayfa adhhab ilā al-maṭʿam?
variations.script: لو سمحت، كيف أذهب إلى المطعم؟
variations.cue: Excuse me, how do I get to the restaurant?
variations.changed: M1's other opener

variations.cue: How do I get to the school?
variations.changed: the bare question, with no opener at all

mistake.why: Going somewhere takes ilā: adhhab ilā al-maḥaṭṭa. Arabic does not let a destination sit bare after the verb.

sentences.usage: The first thing you say in a city you do not know. ʿafwan opens it and the question does the rest.
sentences.mnemonic: Everything in this question is already yours except the place.

words.note: tadhhab with the prefix off and an i- in front, exactly as ishrab was built in M1. The feminine adds -ī.
The al-'d shape of M7's amām, "in front of", and its own index key. With ilā in front it means forward rather than in front of something.

sentences.trap: amām on its own needs something to be in front of. ilā al-amām needs nothing — it is a direction rather than a position.
sentences.sound: IDH-hab, with the dh of English "this". al-a-MĀM, stressed on the long ā.

variations.cue: Go straight ahead, please (to a woman)
variations.changed: the feminine, visible in the romanization and in the script

variations.cue: Go to the station
variations.changed: a place instead of a direction

variations.display: idhhab ilā al-amām thumma ilā as-sūq
variations.script: اذهب إلى الأمام ثم إلى السوق
variations.cue: Go straight ahead and then to the market
variations.changed: thumma from M10 of the level below, chaining two steps

mistake.why: tadhhab is a statement. The command drops the prefix: idhhab.

sentences.usage: Given to a stranger, and this module speaks that way throughout.
sentences.mnemonic: The imperative recipe from M1, on a new verb.

sentences.cue: On the right, then on the left

words.note: The side itself, and ʿalā in front turns it into a direction. y is a moon letter, so the l of al- is written and said.
The partner of al-yamīn, and it behaves identically. Both are nouns, not adverbs, which is why they need ʿalā.

sentences.trap: The sides are NOUNS. English says "turn right" with no preposition and Arabic needs ʿalā, because it is saying "on the right".
sentences.sound: ya-MĪN and ya-SĀR, both stressed on the long vowel of the second syllable.

variations.cue: The restaurant is on the right
variations.changed: the phrase locating something rather than instructing

variations.cue: Go to the left
variations.changed: an imperative in front of the direction

variations.display: al-bayt ʿalā al-yamīn wa al-madrasa ʿalā al-yasār
variations.script: البيت على اليمين والمدرسة على اليسار
variations.cue: The house is on the right and the school is on the left
variations.changed: both sides in one sentence

mistake.why: The side needs ʿalā: ʿalā al-yamīn. Without it you have told someone to go the right itself.

sentences.usage: Half of any real set of directions, and the half a learner has to be able to HEAR rather than say.
sentences.mnemonic: The sides are places, so they need a preposition.

sentences.cue: Take the bus to the market

words.note: An imperative that loses more than its prefix — the hamza of the root goes too, leaving three letters. Learn the shape rather than deriving it.
The MSA word, understood everywhere and written in every newspaper. Every passenger in every Arab city says al-bāṣ instead — that word is named here and appears in no sentence of this course.

sentences.trap: The word you will read and the word you will hear are different words. This module writes the first and tells you about the second, and does so exactly once.
sentences.sound: KHUDH, one syllable, opening with the kh of Scottish "loch" and closing with the dh of "this".

variations.cue: Take the train to the school
variations.changed: another way of getting there

variations.cue: Take the bus, please (to a woman)
variations.changed: the feminine imperative

variations.cue: Take the key, please
variations.changed: the verb doing its ordinary job, with M7's key

mistake.why: That is a statement — "you take". The imperative is khudh, and it is shorter than the rule would predict.

sentences.usage: Advice rather than an instruction. The destination after ilā is what makes it useful.
sentences.mnemonic: One word you write, another you hear.

words.note: The partner of M7's hunāka, "there". Two words, one letter apart in the script, and the difference is the whole distance.

sentences.trap: qarība takes min, not ilā. Arabic measures nearness FROM a place, where English measures it to one.
sentences.sound: hu-NĀ, with the stress on the long final ā.

variations.cue: The restaurant is near here
variations.changed: a masculine place, so the adjective moves

variations.cue: The station is over there
variations.changed: hunāka, and no adjective needed at all

variations.cue: The houses are near the station
variations.changed: M3's non-human plural, taking the feminine singular

mistake.why: Nearness takes min: qarība min hunā. ilā is for going, not for being close.

sentences.usage: Reassurance, and the answer that ends most of the exchanges in this module.
sentences.mnemonic: Near FROM here, not near to it.

sentences.cue: I go by bus every day

words.note: The bi- that has been hiding inside bi-khayr since M2 and bi-kam since M8, doing its own job at last: by, with, for. The row for al-ḥāfila is S04's.

sentences.trap: It is written in full and said as one: bil-ḥāfila. The course never writes the elision, because writing both spellings would give the index two words for one.
sentences.sound: bil-ḤĀ-fi-la — the a of al- vanishes entirely in speech, and the script shows the join.

variations.cue: I go by train every day
variations.changed: another means of travel

variations.cue: I go to work by bus
variations.changed: a destination as well as a means

variations.cue: Do you go by bus?
variations.changed: asked as a question, with M4's ta- form

mistake.why: The course writes the elision out: bi-al-ḥāfila. The Arabic line joins them; the romanized line does not.

sentences.usage: A daily routine, in a module about finding your way. The frame is L1-M4's and only the means is new.

words.note: Masculine. The q is made at the very back of the throat and the ṭ is emphatic, so the whole word sits low.
Ends in ʿayn, which is a letter and not a punctuation mark. sarīʿa for a feminine thing.

sentences.trap: A sentence with no verb again, and by now that should feel ordinary rather than missing.
sentences.sound: sa-RĪʿ, and the final ʿayn is a tightening of the throat after the long ī — not silence.

variations.cue: The bus is fast
variations.changed: a feminine thing, so the adjective moves

variations.cue: The new train is fast
variations.changed: M3's definiteness rule, with the attributive taking al-

variations.cue: The train is fast and the bus is close
variations.changed: two verbless clauses joined by wa

mistake.why: With al- on both it is a phrase — "the fast train" — and there is no sentence. M3's rule, still binding.

sentences.usage: Why you were told to take it. The reason usually follows the advice in an Arabic direction.
sentences.mnemonic: Drop the al- and you have said is.

sentences.cue: The restaurant is next to the station

words.note: Literally "by the side of", and the bi- is S06's. jānib is the side itself, and the two together make a preposition.

sentences.trap: bi-jānib takes the noun straight after it with no min and no ilā. It is already a preposition, and adding another would be doubling.
sentences.sound: bi-JĀ-nib, with the stress on the long ā.

variations.cue: The house is next to the school
variations.changed: another pair of places

variations.cue: The restaurant is next to the market
variations.changed: a landmark from the level below

variations.cue: There's a restaurant next to the station
variations.changed: hunāka doing existential work rather than pointing

mistake.why: bi-jānib is already a preposition. The noun follows it directly.

sentences.usage: How anywhere is located in Arabic: by reference to somewhere else you already know.
sentences.mnemonic: By the side of, and nothing in between.

sentences.cue: There's a restaurant near the house

words.note: M7's row, doing a second job: at the head of a sentence it announces that something exists, and English's "there is" happens to work the same way. The pointing sense is still there too.

sentences.trap: maṭʿam has no al-, and that is what makes the sentence an announcement rather than a location. Adding one would say "the restaurant is there".
sentences.sound: hu-NĀ-ka, one syllable longer than hunā and the same word underneath.

variations.cue: There's a station near here
variations.changed: a feminine place, so the adjective moves

variations.cue: The restaurant is over there
variations.changed: the pointing sense, with the noun definite

variations.cue: Is there a restaurant nearby?
variations.changed: asked as a question, with M2's hal

mistake.why: An announcement takes an indefinite noun: hunāka maṭʿam. With al- the sentence is about a restaurant you both already know.

sentences.usage: The answer to the question in the last variation, which is how you find anything anywhere.
sentences.mnemonic: No al- means it is news.

sentences.cue: Go here and then take the train

words.note: M10's row from the level below, joining two steps in order. Unlike wa it says which came first.

sentences.trap: Nothing new. Two imperatives from this module and one joiner from the last, and that is a whole set of directions.
sentences.sound: THUM-ma, with the th of "think" and the m held long.

variations.display: idhhab ilā al-amām thumma khudh al-ḥāfila
variations.script: اذهب إلى الأمام ثم خذ الحافلة
variations.cue: Go straight ahead and then take the bus
variations.changed: the module's two other frames, chained

variations.display: khudh al-qiṭār thumma idhhab ʿalā al-yamīn
variations.script: خذ القطار ثم اذهب على اليمين
variations.cue: Take the train and then go to the right
variations.changed: the two steps in the other order

variations.cue: Go here and then take the train (to a woman)
variations.changed: both imperatives move to the feminine

mistake.display: idhhab hunā wa thumma khudh al-qiṭār
mistake.why: thumma already joins. Putting wa in front of it doubles the joiner.

sentences.usage: The whole module in one sentence, and it opens nothing new — which is what the last rung of a module should do.

comprehensionPool.cue: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
On the right, then on the left
Take the bus to the market
I go by bus every day
The restaurant is next to the station
There's a restaurant near the house
Go here and then take the train
The house is next to the school
